properties.title: Mainland drainage inspection
properties.text: The fictional mainland inspection found blocked culverts along the canal approach. Crews should remove plastic waste and accumulated sediment before the wet-season exercise. The maintenance plan prioritizes clearing the inlet grates, photographing each obstruction, and logging downstream water levels after cleaning. No pump purchase was approved. This brief recommends a follow-up inspection within seven days of the exercise. The record describes a training scenario and does not establish actual flood conditions in Lagos. Inspectors should attach before-and-after photographs to the same work order so the follow-up team can distinguish repeat blockage from incomplete clearance. The exercise supervisor signs off only after the inlet and outlet have both been checked.

properties.title: Island pump readiness
properties.text: The fictional island response depot has two portable pumps reserved for stormwater exercises. Operators must test hoses and fuel supply before deployment. The staging point is inland from the shoreline. The exercise plan assigns a safety observer to each pump team and prohibits pumping into an already obstructed drain. This is a preparedness inventory, not a live emergency notice.

properties.title: Archived mainland drainage inspection
properties.text: An earlier fictional drainage inspection recommended purchasing a fixed pump and widening the canal inlet. The proposal was exploratory and had no funding decision. This archived brief predates the current maintenance exercise and must not be substituted for the June 2026 clearance plan. Dates matter because historical recommendations can conflict with current instructions.

properties.title: Central district drainage inspection
properties.text: The fictional central district drainage team should replace a collapsed concrete culvert. Removing surface litter alone will not restore the crossing because a structural panel has failed. The exercise budget covers a temporary bypass and an engineering survey. The replacement is scheduled after survey approval. These actions belong to the Abuja exercise area, not the mainland Lagos plan.

properties.title: Southern drainage access
properties.text: The fictional southern drainage inspection concerns access to a tidal outfall. Crews should check the flap gate at low tide and clear vegetation around the maintenance platform. A mobile barrier marks the slippery approach. The exercise coordinator must confirm tide timing before dispatch. Replacing an inland culvert is outside this record's work order.

properties.title: Mainland feeder reliability
properties.text: The fictional mainland electricity feeder has three recurring voltage-drop reports during the evening exercise. The engineering recommendation is to rebalance phase loads before considering transformer replacement. Meter readings must be captured at both ends of the feeder. The planning worksheet assigns phase balancing to the first maintenance window and leaves capital upgrades pending measurement. No actual customer or utility network is represented.

properties.title: Northern feeder reliability
properties.text: The fictional northern feeder inspection found cracked insulators near the training substation. The recommended work is insulator replacement under an approved isolation procedure. Voltage balancing is not the primary fault in this brief. The maintenance team records component serial numbers and photographs after replacement. The location anchor is approximate and is not an actual asset.

properties.title: Mainland drinking-water maintenance
properties.text: The fictional water maintenance team plans to replace leaking service valves near the training junction. After repairs, operators flush the affected section and collect water-quality samples. The brief does not report contamination or certify water as safe. Any real drinking-water decision requires current accredited testing. The exercise inventory lists six replacement valves and two sampling kits.

properties.title: Reservoir instrumentation exercise
properties.text: The fictional reservoir exercise focuses on level-sensor calibration. Technicians compare the telemetry reading with a manual staff-gauge reading before changing alarm thresholds. The plan provides a reference checklist and requires a second operator to verify the offset. Valve replacement is not part of this work order. This record is a training brief, not a reservoir operating instruction.

properties.title: Mainland shade corridor
properties.text: The fictional heat adaptation plan prioritizes shade trees and covered waiting areas along a walking corridor. A field team records canopy cover and surface temperature at fixed times. The proposed pilot uses three observation points and repeats measurements after planting. The brief contains no measured reduction in temperature and makes no claim of demonstrated effectiveness.

properties.title: Northern market shade trial
properties.text: The fictional northern market trial uses removable shade fabric above a pedestrian queue. Observers record queue length and shaded pavement temperature. Permanent tree planting is not proposed because the exercise site has underground service constraints. Trial results are not yet available. The planning record must not be interpreted as a real heat-health advisory.

properties.title: Island bus access review
properties.text: The fictional island bus access review recommends moving the temporary boarding point away from a drainage inlet. A marked pedestrian route should connect the stop to the exercise entrance. The review records accessibility observations rather than ridership forecasts. It does not authorize road construction or changes to a real public transit service.

properties.title: Central shuttle scheduling
properties.text: The fictional central shuttle exercise tests a fifteen-minute departure interval. Dispatchers record boarding duration and departure delay at two temporary stops. The recommendation is to adjust the timetable only after observing the complete morning session. Moving a drainage inlet is outside the trial. No published real-world timetable is represented by this record.

properties.title: Coastal erosion survey plan
properties.text: The fictional coastal survey plan calls for repeat shoreline photographs from fixed observation stations. Surveyors must record tidal stage and camera direction with each image. The brief proposes comparison of shoreline positions after the exercise but reports no erosion rate. Hard coastal defenses are not recommended without a separate engineering and environmental assessment.

properties.title: Wetland vegetation mapping
properties.text: The fictional wetland mapping exercise separates mangrove canopy from open water using field photographs and a small labeled image set. Analysts should check cloud shadows before accepting a water classification. The brief proposes manual review of uncertain pixels and reports no model accuracy. The location identifies an exercise area, not a surveyed habitat boundary.

properties.title: Road crossing inspection
properties.text: The fictional road crossing inspection recommends repainting pedestrian markings and checking the visibility of the exercise sign. Observers log conflicts between turning vehicles and walking participants. No traffic accident statistics were collected. The recommendation is limited to an exercise layout and is not a road-safety certification.

properties.title: Waste collection routing
properties.text: The fictional waste collection exercise compares two routes to a temporary transfer point. Dispatchers should record travel time and container fill level at each stop. No optimized route has been selected yet. The brief asks analysts to keep raw observations so that routing decisions can be checked against measured travel times rather than assumed road speeds.

properties.title: Slope vegetation inspection
properties.text: The fictional slope inspection documents bare soil patches beside a training footpath. The proposed response is to restore vegetation and divert exercise foot traffic until the surface is stable. A geotechnical assessment would be required for any structural intervention. This record provides no landslide probability and should not be used for real slope-risk decisions.

properties.title: Eastern Pacific monitoring buoy
properties.text: The fictional eastern Pacific buoy stores sea-surface temperature observations for an instrumentation exercise. The operator checks battery voltage before downloading the log. The anchor lies east of the international date line and is included to test wrapped geographic queries. No actual buoy or ocean measurement is represented.

properties.title: Western Pacific monitoring buoy
properties.text: The fictional western Pacific buoy stores salinity observations for an instrumentation exercise. The operator cleans the conductivity probe before the calibration check. The anchor lies west of the international date line and must be retrieved by a bounding box crossing that meridian. No actual salinity reading is included in the fixture.
